hypotheses.observation: The workload has 11 elementwise operations over a 64 MiB tensor, but kernel count and memory behavior are unknown.
hypotheses.mechanism: Fusion could reduce intermediate memory traffic and launch overhead only if the operations are split across multiple kernels with materialized intermediates.
hypotheses.transformation: Defer elementwise fusion until kernel boundaries and intermediate materialization are measured.
preconditions: More than one relevant kernel exists.
Intermediate results are written to and reread from memory.
Fusion preserves required synchronization and numerical behavior.
hypotheses.expected_effect: If preconditions hold, lower memory transactions and launch overhead may reduce latency; otherwise benefit is uncertain.
risks: Fusion may increase register pressure or reduce occupancy.
Fusion may be ineffective if operations are already fused or bandwidth is not limiting.
required_evidence: Per-kernel breakdown and intermediate tensor traffic

hypotheses.observation: The reported 0.31 ms boundary latency includes an asynchronous producer and consumer.
hypotheses.mechanism: The measurement may include overlap, queueing, or synchronization effects, so it cannot currently be attributed to a specific kernel or transfer.
hypotheses.transformation: Use producer/consumer GPU event timing and synchronization analysis to decompose the boundary latency before selecting an optimization.
preconditions: Producer and consumer boundaries can be instrumented independently.
The timing method distinguishes queued execution from completed execution.
hypotheses.expected_effect: The decomposition would identify whether launch, memory movement, producer work, consumer work, or synchronization dominates.
risks: Added instrumentation may perturb scheduling or overlap.
Incorrect event placement may still include asynchronous work.
unknowns: Which operations are inside the timed boundary
required_evidence: Independent producer and consumer completion timestamps

hypotheses.observation: The available facts do not establish whether the workload is memory-bound, compute-bound, or occupancy-limited.
hypotheses.mechanism: Memory transactions, cache hit rate, arithmetic intensity, and achieved occupancy are all unknown, so choosing a memory-layout, launch-configuration, or arithmetic transformation would be speculative.
hypotheses.transformation: Defer bottleneck-specific transformation and first collect transaction, cache, arithmetic-intensity, and occupancy measurements.
preconditions: Metrics are collected for the same input size and timing scope as the 0.31 ms observation.
The measurements distinguish the relevant producer and consumer kernels.
hypotheses.expected_effect: The measurements would distinguish whether to prioritize memory-traffic reduction, computation reduction, or resource/occupancy tuning.
risks: Profiler metrics may have measurement overhead or scope mismatch.
